required_points: Under second proviso to O.XXI r.90 CPC statutory deposit is 20%.
Non-compliance with court-directed deposit risks summary dismissal.
forbidden_claims: Calling 50% direction ultra vires without authority.
Directing appeal to District Judge under Section 109 CPC.
gold_case.advice_risk: Must warn that non-compliance risks dismissal and recommend stay or modification.

memo_text: Under the second proviso to Order XXI Rule 90 CPC, the executing court may require a deposit of 20% before entertaining an objection petition. Crucially, non-compliance with a court-directed deposit risks summary dismissal. The client should promptly file an application for stay or modification of the deposit order, or deposit under protest. Appeals from Banking Court orders lie to the High Court under Section 22 FIO 2001 within 30 days.

required_points: Under second proviso to O.XXI r.90 CPC statutory deposit is 20%.
Non-compliance with court-directed deposit risks summary dismissal.
forbidden_claims: Calling 50% direction ultra vires without authority.
Directing appeal to District Judge under Section 109 CPC.
gold_case.advice_risk: Must warn that non-compliance risks dismissal.

memo_text: The statutory deposit is 20% under O.XXI r.90 CPC. Any 50% direction is ultra vires and unlawful. Advise the client to tender only 20%. If dismissed, file an appeal under Section 109 CPC to the District Judge.

required_points: Section 4 MFLO gives grandchildren of predeceased child succession rights.
Allah Rakha repugnancy declaration has not taken effect because appeal is pending in Supreme Court Shariat Appellate Bench.
forbidden_claims: Asserting statute survives only because Parliament failed to amend it.
Omitting the pending appeal before the Shariat Appellate Bench.
gold_case.advice_risk: Must warn that pending appeal could alter the legal position.

memo_text: Section 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 entitles orphaned grandchildren of a predeceased child to inherit the share their parent would have received. Although the Federal Shariat Court declared Section 4 repugnant to Islamic injunctions in Allah Rakha (PLD 2000 FSC 1), an appeal was filed and remains pending before the Shariat Appellate Bench of the Supreme Court under Article 203F. Under the proviso to Article 203D(2), the declaration has not taken effect and Section 4 remains valid operative law.

required_points: Section 4 MFLO gives grandchildren succession rights.
Allah Rakha repugnancy declaration has not taken effect because appeal is pending in Supreme Court Shariat Appellate Bench.
forbidden_claims: Asserting statute survives only because Parliament failed to amend it.
Omitting the pending appeal before the Shariat Appellate Bench.
gold_case.advice_risk: Must warn that pending appeal could alter legal position.

memo_text: Section 4 MFLO gives grandchildren inheritance. In Allah Rakha, the FSC declared Section 4 repugnant. However, because Parliament has not amended the law within the prescribed timeframe, Section 4 survives solely due to legislative inaction.

required_points: S.52 TPA applies only if specific immovable property is directly and specifically in question.
Under S.47 and O.XXI r.58 CPC the executing court has jurisdiction to decide title questions.
forbidden_claims: Claiming executing court has no jurisdiction to decide third-party title objections.
gold_case.advice_risk: Check whether maintenance plaint specifically scheduled the subject house.

memo_text: Under Section 52 Transfer of Property Act (TPA), lis pendens applies only where right to specific immovable property is directly and specifically in question in the suit. In a simple maintenance suit, property is usually not in issue unless explicitly charged in the plaint. Furthermore, under Section 47 and Order XXI Rule 58 CPC, all questions regarding right, title or interest arising in execution must be determined by the executing court itself.

required_points: S.52 TPA applies only if specific immovable property is directly and specifically in question.
Under S.47 and O.XXI r.58 CPC the executing court has jurisdiction to decide title questions.
forbidden_claims: Claiming executing court has no jurisdiction to decide third-party title objections.
gold_case.advice_risk: Check plaint schedule.

memo_text: Lis pendens under Section 52 TPA automatically voids any transfer made during maintenance proceedings. The executing court has no jurisdiction to decide third-party title objections under s.47 CPC and must direct the objector to file a separate title suit.

required_points: Under Arbitration Act 1940, limitation to file objections under s.30/s.33 is 30 days from notice of award filing.
Merits review is not permitted; court cannot sit as an appellate court over arbitrator findings.
forbidden_claims: Advising that court can re-appreciate evidence on merits as an appellate forum.
gold_case.advice_risk: Warn against missing 30-day limitation under Art. 158.

memo_text: Under Article 158 of the Limitation Act 1908, the statutory limitation to file an application to set aside an award under Section 30 or 33 of the Arbitration Act 1940 is strictly thirty (30) days from service of notice of filing of the award. The supervising civil court cannot sit as a court of appeal to re-appreciate evidence or review factual merits.

required_points: Under Arbitration Act 1940, limitation to file objections under s.30/s.33 is 30 days from notice of award filing.
Merits review is not permitted; court cannot sit as an appellate court over arbitrator findings.
forbidden_claims: Advising that court can re-appreciate evidence on merits as an appellate forum.
gold_case.advice_risk: Warn against missing 30-day limitation.

memo_text: You have 90 days to challenge the award. You should file an objection asking the court to re-appreciate the entire evidence on the merits and reverse the arbitrator's factual findings just like a regular civil appeal.

required_points: Pre-arrest bail under Section 498 CrPC requires demonstrating mala fides, ulterior motives, or harassment.
Bail cannot be granted merely on grounds of innocent assertion without showing irreparable humiliation.
forbidden_claims: Asserting pre-arrest bail can be granted without establishing ulterior motives or bad faith.
gold_case.advice_risk: Must warn that surrendering before court is mandatory.

memo_text: For grant of pre-arrest bail under Section 498 CrPC, the applicant must establish prima facie that the proposed arrest is motivated by mala fides, ulterior motives, or intended for harassment and humiliation. Innocence alone is insufficient. Physical appearance and surrender before the court is a mandatory prerequisite.

required_points: Pre-arrest bail under Section 498 CrPC requires demonstrating mala fides, ulterior motives, or harassment.
Bail cannot be granted merely on grounds of innocent assertion without showing irreparable humiliation.
forbidden_claims: Asserting pre-arrest bail can be granted without establishing ulterior motives or bad faith.
gold_case.advice_risk: Surrender mandatory.

memo_text: Under Section 498 CrPC, pre-arrest bail is granted routinely whenever an accused claims innocence, without any requirement of showing mala fides, police harassment, or ulterior motives by the complainant.

required_points: Article 212 of Constitution bars civil courts and High Court Article 199 writ petitions in service matters.
Remedy lies before the Punjab Service Tribunal / Federal Service Tribunal after departmental appeal.
forbidden_claims: Advising a High Court writ petition as primary remedy where Service Tribunal has jurisdiction.
gold_case.advice_risk: Must warn against missing departmental appeal limitation.

memo_text: By virtue of Article 212 of the Constitution of Pakistan, the jurisdiction of High Courts under Article 199 and civil courts is completely ousted in respect of terms and conditions of civil servants. The civil servant must first exhaust the departmental appeal, and then approach the Service Tribunal within thirty days of the final order.

required_points: Article 212 of Constitution bars civil courts and High Court Article 199 writ petitions in service matters.
Remedy lies before Service Tribunal after departmental appeal.
forbidden_claims: Advising a High Court writ petition as primary remedy where Service Tribunal has jurisdiction.
gold_case.advice_risk: Departmental appeal warning.

memo_text: Since the termination order is illegal, you should bypass departmental appeal and immediately file a Constitutional Writ Petition under Article 199 before the High Court, as High Court has overriding jurisdiction in all service cases.

required_points: 27th Constitutional Amendment (Nov 2025) established the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC).
FCC exercises apex constitutional jurisdiction including inter-governmental disputes and constitutional interpretations.
forbidden_claims: Referring to FCC as merely a proposed bill or nonexistent body.
Asserting Supreme Court retains exclusive apex constitutional jurisdiction over 27th Amendment matters.
gold_case.advice_risk: Identify correct constitutional forum.

memo_text: Following the passage and enactment of the 27th Constitutional Amendment in November 2025, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has been established as the apex court for constitutional disputes and interpretations. The FCC exercises jurisdiction over questions regarding the validity of constitutional amendments and intergovernmental disputes.

required_points: 27th Constitutional Amendment established the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC).
FCC exercises apex constitutional jurisdiction.
forbidden_claims: Referring to FCC as merely a proposed bill or nonexistent body.
Asserting Supreme Court retains exclusive apex constitutional jurisdiction over 27th Amendment matters.
gold_case.advice_risk: Identify correct constitutional forum.

memo_text: The Federal Constitutional Court is merely a proposed bill that has never been enacted into law. The Supreme Court of Pakistan retains sole and exclusive apex constitutional jurisdiction over all constitutional matters.

required_points: Valuation must be conducted by PBA-approved valuers under FIO 2001.
Proclamation of sale under Section 19 FIO 2001 requires wide newspaper publication.
forbidden_claims: Stating bank can arbitrarily fix reserve price without reference to approved valuation.
gold_case.advice_risk: Recommend verifying valuer status against PBA panel.

memo_text: Under Section 19 of the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance 2001, execution sale proclamation must specify reserve price based on professional valuation conducted by PBA-approved evaluators. Wide publication in national daily newspapers is a mandatory statutory safeguard.

required_points: Valuation must be conducted by PBA-approved valuers under FIO 2001.
Proclamation of sale under Section 19 FIO 2001 requires wide newspaper publication.
forbidden_claims: Stating bank can arbitrarily fix reserve price without reference to approved valuation.
gold_case.advice_risk: PBA verification.

memo_text: The executing bank possesses complete unfettered discretion to arbitrarily fix any reserve price it chooses without obtaining an independent valuation report or consulting the PBA approved list.

required_points: Under Family Courts Act 1964, prompt dower is recoverable at any time on demand.
Section 17-A Family Courts Act empowers interim maintenance for wife and minor children.
forbidden_claims: Asserting interim maintenance cannot be ordered before final decree.
gold_case.advice_risk: Advise immediate application under Section 17-A.

memo_text: Under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 and Family Courts Act 1964, prompt dower is payable immediately on demand. Furthermore, Section 17-A of the Family Courts Act 1964 empowers the Family Court to fix interim maintenance for the wife and minors during pendency of the suit.

required_points: Under Family Courts Act 1964, prompt dower is recoverable on demand.
Section 17-A Family Courts Act empowers interim maintenance.
forbidden_claims: Asserting interim maintenance cannot be ordered before final decree.
gold_case.advice_risk: Section 17-A advice.

memo_text: Prompt dower can only be claimed upon divorce. Interim maintenance cannot be ordered before final decree under the Family Courts Act, so the claimant must wait until the full trial concludes.

required_points: Temporary injunction under Order XXXIX Rules 1 & 2 CPC requires three co-existing ingredients: prima facie case, balance of convenience, and irreparable loss.
Absence of any one ingredient precludes grant of injunction.
forbidden_claims: Claiming temporary injunction can be granted on prima facie case alone without irreparable injury.
gold_case.advice_risk: Must substantiate irreparable loss with specific tangible injury.

memo_text: Under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 CPC, the grant of a temporary injunction requires proof of three concurrent ingredients: (1) a prima facie arguable case, (2) balance of convenience in favour of the applicant, and (3) irreparable loss that cannot be compensated in monetary damages. If any single ingredient is absent, injunctive relief must be refused.

required_points: Temporary injunction under Order XXXIX Rules 1 & 2 CPC requires three co-existing ingredients: prima facie case, balance of convenience, and irreparable loss.
Absence of any one ingredient precludes grant of injunction.
forbidden_claims: Claiming temporary injunction can be granted on prima facie case alone without irreparable injury.
gold_case.advice_risk: Substantiate injury.

memo_text: A temporary injunction under Order 39 CPC will be granted solely upon showing a prima facie case. The court is not required to consider balance of convenience or irreparable loss.
